title: observability: token-level KV metrics + tracing + dashboard + alert tuning
author: Riley Chen
release_notes: Add token-level KV cache metrics and tracing hooks; new Grafana dashboard and tuned alert thresholds for KV cache degradation. Backwards-compatible.
description: Summary: Add token-level KV cache metrics, KV-specific tracing spans, a Grafana dashboard for token/KV cost and latency breakdowns, and tuned alert rules for KV cache regressions. Motivation: recent incidents showed KV cache evictions and cold-cache latency spikes that were hard to attribute to specific workloads. This PR instruments token-level metrics and traces so we can correlate latency/cost with cache behavior and prompt patterns. Scope: 1) new metrics exported from the runtime to the observability pipeline (token_kv_cache_hits, token_kv_cache_misses, token_kv_evictions, token_kv_latency_ms); 2) tracing spans around KV lookup/hotpath with attributes for model, route, and token_count; 3) Grafana dashboard with cost/latency breakdowns per token bucket and per-model views; 4) updated Prometheus alert rules with tuned thresholds and alert grouping; 5) docs and runbook updates for incident response. Checklist: - [x] Add metrics in runtime exporter - [x] Add tracing hooks and attributes - [x] Create Grafana dashboard JSON and provisioning - [x] Add Prometheus alert rules and recording rules - [x] Update docs and runbook - [x] End-to-end testing on canary cluster Deployment notes: rollout as follows: (a) deploy runtime changes to canary pool with observability flag enabled; (b) validate metrics and traces in staging dashboards for at least 2 hours under synthetic load; (c) apply alert rules in staging, verify alert firing and silences; (d) promote to production via gradual canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Backwards compatibility: metrics are additive and default to zero if KV not enabled. No schema changes to existing telemetry. Related: ENG-2345 (KV cache regressions), ENG-2401 (observability gaps).
commits: tracing: add KV lookup spans and token_count attribute
monitoring: add recording rules for token-level hit_rate and p95 latency
grafana: add token-kv-overview and per-model panels
alerts: tune KV cache degradation thresholds and grouping
docs: token-level observability and runbook update
review_comments: Aisha Kaur: Please confirm cardinality of the new tags (model, route) under high-traffic workloads - we need to ensure we don't blow up label cardinality in Prometheus.

Riley Chen (author): Good catch - I switched model and route to be recorded as stable low-cardinality labels in recording rules and added a config flag to limit tag resolution in exporter (default: per-model, not per-route).
Diego Martinez: CI initially failed on lint (grafana JSON formatting) and one flaky test. After fixes re-ran CI and all checks passed.
Samir Patel: Alert thresholds look reasonable but please add a short runbook step to validate alert noise when we deploy - also include an escalation target.
Riley Chen (author): Added runbook steps and an escalation contact (oncall-infra). Addressed reviewer comments and rebased onto latest main.
Aisha Kaur: Approving after verifying metrics cardinality and dashboard panels in staging.
ci_summary: Initial CI: 1 failing lint job (grafana JSON) and 1 flaky integration test -> fixes applied. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, e2e canary tests).
testing_notes: Local unit tests + integration canary run against staging observability stack. Synthetic load used to validate p50/p95 token-level latency and hit_rate. Confirmed recording rules reduced cardinality exposure to Prometheus. Deployed to canary for 6 hours with no increase in alert noise.
notes_for_ops: When enabling in prod, set exporter.flag.token_kv_observability=true and exporter.flag.max_tag_resolution=per_model to limit labels. Monitor new recording rules and drop rate; watch for increased Prometheus cardinality. Dashboard panels are provisioned; reload Grafana if necessary.
